messages:
maria: FYI nightly perf/regression spike on multi-GPU inference, p99 latency +2.8% and memory working set up ~600MB across 8 GPUs. Noticed during rerun of GPT-variant benchmark. @sanjay @kevin can you triage?

sanjay: Seen it. Quick profiler dump points at extra transient NCCL allocations around KV-cache eviction boundaries.

kevin: Weird — our NCCL pool sizing shouldn't change across runs. Do we have traces?

maria: Pasted a short perf dump below. Looks like repeated temp tensors in nvtx ranges: "nccl_send/recv_tmp" and "tp_shard_temp" around attention KV flushes.

maria: ```
# perf summary (trimmed)
GPU0  total allocs: 1.9k  transient: 482  peak: 12.7GB
NCCL temp allocs: 142 (avg 3.2MB)  spikes aligned with kv-evict
TP shard temp: 97 allocs (avg 1.6MB)  workspace expand events: 6

nvprof: stack traces show kernel fallback to non-optimized path when workspace smaller than 2MB
```

yun: If kernel is falling back because workspace was too small that would trigger extra mallocs. Are we shrinking workspace after each sequence to free memory?

kevin: We recently changed allocator thresholds to reduce fragmentation (TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF tweak). That lowered steady-state but might cause smaller workspace allocations that trigger kernel fallback.

sanjay: Can confirm. Our change set: `TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=garbage_collection_threshold:0.7,max_split_size_mb:32` — net effect: more aggressive reclamation and smaller contiguous free blocks. Kernel selection code tests workspace size < required -> picks fallback kernel which needs extra temporaries that allocate via cudaMalloc and free.

maria: So two issues chain: allocator tuning -> smaller contiguous workspaces -> kernel fallback -> transient NCCL/temp allocs during KV eviction -> p99 latency + memory churn.

kevin: Proposed mitigations: 1) prefer keeping a small preallocated workspace slab per device for critical kernels (min_workspace=8MB) 2) change kernel selection to prefer optimized kernel and delay fallback if we can reclaim from comm pool 3) reuse NCCL comm buffers across TP shards instead of allocate-per-call.

yun: +1 for preallocated slab. Implementation idea: maintain per-GPU ring of workspace slices that are returned to pool on sequence end, not on every eviction. That avoids split/fragmentation pressure.

sanjay: For NCCL buffers we can move from ephemeral allocs to a shared comm pool sized by max_inflight_tokens * tp_shards. Current code creates `nccl_temp_buf` on demand. Replace with `comm_pool.acquire(size)` and keep it pinned until op finishes.

maria: Does the comm pool already exist? I saw `comm_pool` in an experiment branch but not in main.

kevin: It's in eng-runtime/comm-pool branch. It has API and basic allocator but not integrated with kernel selection or KV eviction path. I can open a PR to wire it into `tp_shard_send_recv` path.

yun: Small experiment suggestion: run benchmark with `TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:256` (looser splitting) and with `REDWOOD_PREALLOC_WORKSPACE=8MB` env to see if p99 drops.

maria: On a quick run with `REDWOOD_PREALLOC_WORKSPACE=8MB` I saw p99 back to baseline and NCCL temp allocs drop by ~90%. But owned GPU peak memory up ~300MB (expected).

sanjay: Tradeoff looks ok if we can bound prealloc. For Dedicated customers we can increase reserved capacity; default hosted could use adaptive policy: prealloc only when throughput pattern shows frequent kernel fallbacks.

kevin: Also worth patching kernel selector to prefer optimized kernel if `workspace_size + comm_pool.available >= required_workspace`. That makes it check both allocator free and comm pool reclaimable buffers.

maria: We should add a regression test: synthetic KV-evict pattern that toggles between short and long sequences to reproduce allocation spikes. Add nvprof/nvtx markers to assert no cudaMallocs in hot path.

yun: I'll draft the test. Also add a flamegraph of memory alloc/free sequences to CI perf job.

sanjay: One more note: NCCL internal temp allocations can be influenced by `NCCL_LAUNCH_MODE` and `NCCL_P2P_LEVEL`. Try `NCCL_LAUNCH_MODE=GROUP` and `NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=PXB` in the repro to see if internal behavior changes.

kevin: Good call. We should also ensure `ncclCommInitRank` is done once per shard/session, not per request. Double-check the lifecycle in tp-shard path.

maria: Action items:
- kevin: PR to wire comm_pool into tp_shard send/recv and kernel selector (ETA 2 days)
- yun: synthetic KV-evict regression test + perf CI hook (ETA 3 days)
- sanjay: experiment configs for allocator envs + NCCL vars and summarize runs (ETA EOD tomorrow)

kevin: Will also add telemetry counters: kernel_fallback_count, comm_pool_hits, transient_cuda_malloc_count so we can monitor in Console.

maria: Sounds good. If anyone hits OOM during tests, try `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` to get cleaner traces, and set `TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=garbage_collection_threshold:0.85` temporarily.

infra-bot: Deploy job started: perf-run/1785123456-repro (this will run the baseline and patched configs).

maria: Thanks. Keeping thread open - will post results here. :eyes:
